activities.caption: rebuild history's slow reveal of the dark sector
activities.name: dmRevealOrder

config.prompt: From suspicion to photograph — order the reveal:
items: 1933: Zwicky — the Coma cluster's galaxies move too fast for their visible mass ('dunkle Materie')
1970s: Rubin and Ford — galaxy rotation curves refuse to fall
The CMB's acoustic peaks split matter into baryonic and dark components cleanly
The Bullet Cluster separates the dark mass from the hot gas — visually
config.why: The same logic once pointed from Uranus's misbehaving orbit to Neptune's position before anyone saw it — here the deviation is measured but the 'Neptune' is still missing.

activities.anchor: a property of empty space itself, whatever that means
activities.caption: pair the 1998 measurement with what it concluded
activities.name: dmAccelMatch

config.prompt: The distance–redshift relationship is where dark energy was found:

pairs.left: distant Type Ia supernovae fainter than predicted
pairs.right: the expansion is speeding up — acceleration, discovered 1998, Nobel 2011

pairs.left: a supernova at z = 0.5 about 25% fainter than matter-only predicts
pairs.right: detectable only because the calibration is that good
Einstein's 'biggest blunder', resurrected — density that does not dilute as space grows
what acceleration requires in the Friedmann equations

config.why: Dark energy is named, not explained: 'dark' because it does not emit or absorb, 'energy' because it behaves like one.

activities.anchor: consistent with the oldest globular clusters and stellar
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the concordance arithmetic
activities.name: dmConcordCloze

config.text: A matter-only universe would be younger than its %%0%% stars. With the measured mix — ~5% baryons, %%1%% per cent dark matter, %%2%% per cent dark energy — the Friedmann equations give 13.8 billion years.
config.hint: The absurdity a matter-only fit creates, and the two numbers that fix it.

activities.anchor: the galaxy we actually live in
activities.caption: bet first — the Keplerian prediction vs the flat truth
activities.name: dmCurvePredict

config.q: In a Keplerian system (all mass central), orbital speed falls with radius. What did Rubin and Ford find for hydrogen clouds far beyond the visible disk?
choices: Speeds holding flat near 200–300 km/s — far past where the visible mass should let them fall
Speeds rising steeply, faster than near the centre
Speeds falling exactly as predicted — the dark matter idea was wrong
config.why: Matching a flat curve at 30 kiloparsecs requires roughly 5–6 times the luminous mass, arranged in a halo extending far beyond the starlight.

activities.anchor: You are not, repeat not, being slowly inflated
activities.caption: true or false — where expansion applies
activities.name: dmExpandJudge

statements.s: Dark energy makes the Solar System and the Milky Way expand too.
statements.why: Inside gravitationally bound systems its influence is roughly a million-billionth of gravity.

statements.s: Expansion applies to unbound space: the emptiness between galaxy clusters.
statements.why: Bound systems never expand — short of a Big Rip, which needs a strengthening dark component.

statements.s: A Big Rip requires a dark component that strengthens over time.
statements.why: Not the constant we measure — w ≈ −1 and holding, with tentative hints that may evolve.

statements.s: The Earth, the Solar System, the Milky Way and the Local Group are not expanding.
statements.why: You are not, repeat not, being slowly inflated.

activities.anchor: a photograph of the dark sector
activities.caption: find the faulty line — structure formation
activities.name: dmStructureSpot

config.prompt: One line of this structure-formation answer is wrong — click it:
lines: The CMB shows density fluctuations of one part in 100,000 at 380,000 years.
In a baryon-only universe, those fluctuations grow easily into today's galaxies.
Dark matter, interacting only gravitationally, began collapsing before the CMB was released.
Baryons fell into those gravitational wells and were amplified — the cosmic web reproduced.
config.correction: Far too small to grow by today in a baryon-only universe — baryons could not even clump before 380,000 years, held up by radiation pressure.
config.why: Without dark matter's head start, the galaxies we observe could not exist — the simulations reproduce the cosmic web only with cold dark matter.

activities.anchor: the search is for a new particle or a new law
activities.caption: fill the blanks — ruling out the hiding places
activities.name: dmBaryonCloze

config.text: Nucleosynthesis plus the CMB fix the total baryon density at about %%0%% per cent of the matter density; dark matter is %%1%% to %%2%% times the baryonic total, and demonstrably non-baryonic.
config.hint: The missing baryons were eventually found — hiding in ionised intergalactic filaments.
